cases.title: Attributing 'chowkidar chor hai' findings to the Supreme Court
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: Hindi/English mixed; exact uninterrupted verbatim transcript pending
cases.medium: remarks to media after Rafale admissibility order
cases.claim_text: Court-recorded description: Rahul Gandhi attributed to the Supreme Court the view that 'Chowkidar (Mr. Narendra Modi, Prime Minister) is a thief'. This is not labeled a verbatim recording transcript.
testable_propositions: The Supreme Court judicially found or endorsed the assertion that Narendra Modi was a thief or guilty of Rafale corruption.
cases.confidence: high on the narrow proposition; original full recording remains to be authenticated
evidence_for: Contemporaneous recorded-video page establishes an attribution was publicly reported; judgment itself describes the attribution.
evidence_against: 15 Apr 2019 Supreme Court order explicitly disclaimed any such finding, limiting the 10 Apr decision to admissibility of documents.
14 Nov 2019 judgment paras 26-33 records attribution, unconditional apology on 8 May, and closure with caution.
cases.counterargument: Gandhi described his rhetoric as heat-of-campaign and said the attribution was unintentional. That speaks to intent, not truth of the attributed judicial finding.
limitations: Whole April 10 recording and surrounding remarks not transcribed
No broader verdict here on merits of the Rafale corruption allegations
cases.next_action: Retrieve Court-hosted 10 Apr, 15 Apr and 14 Nov documents and complete video; submit to human editor

cases.title: Mahadevapura: 1,00,250 allegedly stolen votes
cases.speaker: Rahul Gandhi
cases.original_language: English, based on Congress summary; full unedited video verification pending
cases.medium: press conference, Indira Bhawan, New Delhi
cases.claim_text: Congress-edited highlights: 'approximately 1,00,250 votes were stolen out of 6.5 lakh total votes in Mahadevapura.'
cases.claim_type: quantitative electoral fraud and causal allegation
testable_propositions: Exactly or approximately 100,250 fraudulent ballots were cast or counted in 2024.
Five categories of suspicious electoral roll entries reliably identify unique ineligible voters rather than overlapping entries or stale address records.
The suspicious entries caused the result in Bangalore Central to change.
BJP and ECI intentionally colluded in this alleged manipulation.
cases.confidence: moderate on failure to establish ballot theft, not a finding that rolls were clean
evidence_for: Independent field checks found mass registrations tied to changing-tenancy addresses; irregular/stale entries have support.
Five category totals supplied by Congress sum to 100,250, but arithmetic is not independent verification.
evidence_against: An entry in a voter roll is not proof that a ballot was cast; no identified voter-level ballot reconciliation or deduplicated methodology retrieved.
Mobility and legitimate historic occupancy explain some high address counts, while not dispelling stale/ineligible entries.
CEO Karnataka asked for a sworn particulars-based complaint, which is an institutional response rather than proof of falsity.
limitations: Constituency 2024 source voter roll and supplemental logs not retrieved
Official votes-cast records and tendered-voter/marked-roll information missing
Full original event recording not checked
cases.next_action: Obtain dated 2024 roll snapshots, Form 6/7/8 adjudications, Form 17C and poll-station records where law permits; examine category overlap and turnout
